correctness.summary: Connectivity of the irregular-edge bipartite spanning graph reduces the problem to exact degree-class counts. The cycle-rank identity, parity obstruction for one maximum-degree vertex, equality analysis, and regular-graph constructions prove the formula and classification. Exact finite checks agree.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Chartrand and Zhang (2026) classify the cycle-rank-2 bidegree cases {2,3} and {2,4} and ask about higher cycle rank, but do not state the all-parameter minimum-cycle-rank threshold or extremal classification. The older unrestricted least-size result is explicitly treated as prior art and excluded from the novelty claim.

value.summary: The theorem gives the exact first attainable cycle rank for every two-element positive degree set in the newly introduced LIC setting and completely describes all threshold realizations, directly extending the known rank-2 classification.

limitations: Only two-element positive degree sets are treated.
The theorem determines the minimum attainable cycle rank, not every larger attainable cycle rank.
The unrestricted least-size formula for two-element degree sets is prior art and is not claimed as new.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; recent or differently indexed bidegreed/cyclomatic work remains a residual risk.
Finite computation supports but does not replace the proof.
